Where it began

Zakary Glen Foulkes was born in Christchurch on 5 June 2002, and cricket was always going to be part of the furniture. His father, Glen, and his brothers Liam and Robbie all played for Canterbury Country, so there was rarely a shortage of bowlers in the back garden.

At St Andrew's College he made his name early. In 2019 the school won the Gillette Cup, New Zealand's national secondary schools competition, and he was the side's top run-scorer and top wicket-taker, with 267 runs, a hundred among them, and nine wickets. When he first played for Canterbury Country in the Hawke Cup, in 2021, he made 92 and took six wickets, which is a fairly loud way to introduce yourself.

The player

He is a right-arm medium-pacer who bats right-handed, the kind of cricketer selectors call useful and team-mates call lucky to have. He played his first match for Canterbury in February 2022, made his first-class debut against Auckland a month later and earned his first professional contract that July. In his first Super Smash season he was Canterbury's joint leading wicket-taker, with 12, as they reached the final.

He first played Test cricket in Zimbabwe, in August 2025, and took nine wickets in the match, including five in an innings. At the time no New Zealander had bowled better on Test debut. By November 2026 he had played six Tests and taken 21 wickets at 25.62, with 5 for 37 his best.

What made him special

He has taken wickets at every level he has tried: for his school, for Canterbury Country, in the Super Smash and in Tests. A Test bowling average of 25.62 is a number most seam bowlers would happily sign for.

By November 2026 the batting was a work in progress at Test level: 45 runs, with a top score of 23 not out. But a man who once hit a schoolboy hundred will not be content to stay at the tail for ever.

Away from the middle

The game has taken him a long way from Christchurch. In 2022 he played T20 cricket in Queensland for Wynnum-Manly, had a season with Warwickshire in 2024 and another with Durham after that. In December 2025 Chennai Super Kings picked him up at the auction ahead of the 2026 Indian Premier League season.

And finally

His first one-day international, in Sri Lanka in late 2024, was washed out before he had bowled a ball or picked up a bat. Some debuts are quieter than others, and his Test debut more than made up for it.
